credit.instrument: Long-term bank facilities (Fund-based LT-Cash Credit, INR 25.00 crore)
credit.outlook: Not applicable (Placed on Rating Watch with Developing Implications)
credit.rationale: Ratings placed on Rating Watch with Developing Implications (RWD) pending clarity on the consolidated credit profile, following the announced scheme of amalgamation of AeroStructures Manufacturing India, Aequs Engineered Plastics and Aequs Force Consumer Products into Aequs. | Rating continues to factor in Aequs' established position in aerospace with full value-chain vertical integration and long-term agreements with reputed global customers (Airbus, Mattel), driving consistent order inflows. | Key monitorables are the gradual ramp-up/stabilisation of the large ATP consumer-electronics project and continuous net losses; liquidity is adequate, aided by the ~INR 814 crore raised via IPO/pre-IPO in Q3FY26 used for debt reduction.

deepdive.sec: Aerospace Precision Engineering & Consumer Electronics Contract Manufacturing

bull_bear.body: Prioritizing capacity expansion for confirmed customer demand (Mattel, Apple ecosystem); net debt/equity improved to 0.23x post-IPO; cash balance INR 3,015 Cr; no dividend mentioned, reinvestment mode for growth.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Consumer segment ramp-up delay beyond Q4FY27; dependency on single large consumer electronics customer; geopolitical supply chain disruptions (West Asia) impacting logistics and raw material lead times (Titanium 52 weeks, Steel 65-75 weeks); key management change (CFO stepping down); equipment sourcing constraints from China.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on long-term structural growth and moat (vertical integration, speed-to-market); transparent about short-term P&L pain from consumer capex; pragmatic on working capital buildup due to geopolitical stocking; committed to margin recovery via utilization.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Aerospace segment EBITDA margin of 27% reported includes other income and excludes unallocated corporate costs; true operational margin is ~20%; Consumer electronics and Aerospace share 'precision manufacturing' platform capabilities but use distinct machine bases (CNC for metal/aero/electronics vs. Molding for plastics/toys); PLI benefits only start accruing in FY27.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body: - Vision 2031 targets 20% consolidated ROCE at steady state, with consumer EBITDA breakeven by Q4FY27 and consolidated PAT breakeven by H1FY28, implying disciplined reinvestment for scale.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Aerospace: Revenue INR 10,464 Cr (+27% YoY), EBITDA INR 2,813 Cr (+76% YoY), ROCE 20%. Consumer: Revenue INR 1,840 Cr (+84% YoY), EBITDA Loss INR 783 Cr (loss widened due to new capacity commissioning); utilization currently 23%, targeting 40-50% in FY27.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply chain de-risking and China+1 strategy driving orders to India | Aequs Limited | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of global OEMs shifting sourcing to India; unique position with vertically integrated capabilities and large order book. |
| Raw material inflation and logistics disruption | Indian Aerospace Suppliers without long-term contracts | loser | Med | Players without pass-through mechanisms or long-term material coverage will suffer margin compression from titanium/steel price spikes and logistics delays. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- India's first and only vertically integrated aerospace manufacturing ecosystem, co-locating forging, machining, surface treatment, and assembly on a single campus to compress supply chains and reduce customer risk.
- Differentiated by a replicable campus model with >50% cluster value add, institutional process repeatability, and long-term OEM partnerships (Airbus, Boeing, Safran, Collins).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [JV] Ajna Aerospace & Defence JV (Jan 2026) with Accel India and Vagus Defence to manufacture UAVs, leveraging battle-proven IP and targeting India's $22B capital acquisition pool.
- [JV] 50:50 JV with Tramontina (2024) for premium cookware, leveraging Aequs' local presence and regulatory expertise for faster industrialization.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Aerospace margins sustained at ~20% operational level despite mix changes; Consumer margins depressed by low utilization (23%) and high fixed depreciation; material cost inflation (titanium/steel) passed through to customers via long-term agreements; logistics costs up slightly due to West Asia crisis but deemed non-material.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: FY27 Revenue Growth: 45-50% consolidated (Aerospace 25-30%, Consumer 125-150%); Margins: Aerospace ~20% EBITDA, Consumer to reach EBITDA breakeven by Q4FY27; Order Inflow: Continued addition of 100+ SKUs/quarter in Aerospace; Capex: INR 660 Cr total (INR 160 Cr Aerospace, INR 500 Cr Consumer).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: $889 million in Aerospace (approx. 8-9x trailing aerospace revenue); robust visibility driven by 433 new parts added in Q4 alone (total portfolio 5,654 SKUs); long-term agreements with global OEMs for engine and landing gear components.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: New INR 1,900 Cr MoU for vertically integrated aero-engine/landing gear park in Hosur (Tamil Nadu); INR 2,856 Cr expansion in Belagavi/Hubballi; moving up value chain into engine components (revenue impact from FY28); PLI scheme eligibility starting FY27.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Aequs delivered a landmark FY26 with 33% revenue growth and a $889M aerospace order book, but consolidated PAT remains negative due to aggressive consumer electronics capex depreciation. The investment thesis hinges on achieving consumer EBITDA breakeven by Q4FY27 and sustaining 20%+ aerospace margins as new Hosur and Karnataka capacities commission.

verdicts.item: Aerospace EBITDA margins to remain in the 20%-plus range going forward (nine-month FY26 at 24%).
verdicts.note: Aravind Melligeri: '...maintaining EBITDA numbers at about 20% level.' and 'Our focus remains on maintaining operating margins at around the 20% level.'

verdicts.item: Aerospace business has opportunity to grow north of 20% (revenue).
verdicts.note: Aravind Melligeri: '...should deliver 25% to 30% revenue growth...' and 'The 20-plus percent is what we have guided in the past, in the long-term'

verdicts.item: Consumer segment utilisation at 31%, expected to improve quarterly, driving better EBITDA and profitability.
verdicts.note: Rajeev Kaul: 'Our primary focus this year will be driving capacity utilization from 23% today to a target of 40% to 50% by the year end.' Utilization is 23%, not 31%.

verdicts.item: Pre-IPO guidance for overall PAT-positive by end of FY27 is being re-evaluated; management declined to reaffirm the timeline pending consumer electronics capacity decisions.
verdicts.note: Rajeev Kaul: 'we fully expect to see consolidated PAT hit break-even by H1 FY28.' Timeline pushed from FY27 to H1 FY28.

verdicts.item: Stated priorities: (1) grow aerospace profitably, (2) drive consumer utilisation via customer additions, (3) pursue aerospace-defense opportunities.
verdicts.note: Aravind Melligeri: 'First, is to continue to grow aerospace revenues profitably... Second, drive consumer utilization... Third, move our consumer EBITDA to break even...' and 'we are actively moving u…

verdicts.item: Expanding aerospace portfolio into higher-value landing gear and engine components, leveraging integrated forging, machining and surface treatment.
verdicts.note: Rajeev Kaul: 'We're also actively moving up the value chain into landing gear and engine components, where our integrated forging, machining, and surface treatment capabilities deliver significant com…

verdicts.item: Most FY26 capex already done; no significant new capex expected this year, only some capitalization spilling into Q4 (mainly consumer electronics).
verdicts.note: Management guided INR500 crores consumer capex and INR160 crores aerospace capex for FY27, indicating significant new capex, contradicting 'no significant new capex expected this year'.

verdicts.item: Long-run goal to balance consumer and aerospace revenue by scaling consumer faster, with both segments converging to similar margin profiles at scale.
verdicts.note: Aravind Melligeri: 'In consumer, we have guided the similar margins as the aerospace, overall 20% EBITDA is our long-term goal.' and 'we are building a precision manufacturing platform here.'
